source.title: TopoAlign: Topology-Aware Visual Representation Alignment
source.authors: Xinyuan Yan; Rita Sevastjanova; Mennatallah El-Assady; Bei Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures and visualizes topological correspondences between representations, but it does not test whether alignment increases with scale or capability, whether cross-modal alignment rises as models improve, or any other listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative mapper-graph comparisons across training epochs, layers, model sizes, and modalities. These are findings about topological organization, not tests of the listed convergence trends or of similarity under alternative metrics. The paper also describes changing layout/alignment parameters, including λ, but those settings illustrate the proposed visualization method rather than measure naturally arising representational convergence. Prediction-accuracy examples are omitted because they are not alignment measures.
record.test_reason: This is a visualization-method paper (TopoAlign). It uses mapper graphs to compare representations across fine-tuning epochs, layers, BERT-base vs BERT-Tiny, and CLIP image vs caption embeddings. All comparisons are qualitative case studies. None measures whether alignment between independently trained models rises with scale or capability, or across seeds. None tests linear mappability, universal features, or metric dependence of convergence. CLIP's two modalities are trained jointly and contrastively, so their correspondence does not test V2. The record's T6 assignment and its 'none' links for all rows are correct.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors present TopoAlign as a topology-aware visual framework. They say it reveals meaningful structural patterns, such as splitting, merging and disentanglement, across training stages, layers, models and modalities, supported by preliminary feedback from five experts. They make no claim about convergence with scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces a mapper-graph and visualization-based method for comparing topological structure, rather than reproducing the original sources’ convergence measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper shows that changing global layout strength λ changes how strongly corresponding nodes are visually pulled together. It also describes interactive adjustment of intra- and inter-graph clustering weights, but does not report a systematic sensitivity study of convergence outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Mapper-graph structure of fine-tuned BERT representations changes across epochs (mixed categories separate), across layers (lexical to semantic grouping), and across model size (BERT-Tiny more entangled).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Topological organization of fine-tuned word representations becomes more category-separated with training, depth and model size.

fits_no_version.finding: CLIP image and caption mapper graphs share a chain-like global topology but differ locally in concept grouping and granularity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a contrastively trained vision-language model, the two modalities share global topology but differ locally.

record.problems: The alignment findings are predominantly qualitative and based on mapper graphs; no overall numerical alignment score or uncertainty estimates are reported. The model-size comparison covers BERT-base and BERT-Tiny in one task, and the cross-modal comparison covers one CLIP setup and one dataset. The authors also note that local alignment discovery can produce low-quality alignments when representation spaces differ substantially.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows were added for individual illustrative local patterns or prediction-accuracy examples; they are case-level examples rather than separate reported alignment metrics. The λ layout illustrations are described in gate_note because they demonstrate the visualization parameter, not natural convergence.

untested.parts: No sweep over scale or capability, and no alignment measure between independently trained models. The BERT-base vs BERT-Tiny comparison is qualitative only.
There is only one CLIP model, trained jointly, so it cannot show alignment rising as separately trained vision and language models improve.
No models from different seeds are compared.
There is no mapping, stitching or relative-representation test. The 'global alignment' is a graph-layout force, not a map between representations.
No cross-model test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Convergence outcomes are never compared under different similarity metrics or inputs. λ and the edge weights only change the visual layout and clustering.
No overall alignment level, plateau or causal explanation is tested.

record.verdict_notes: The relation could arguably be cites_only. The paper cites convergence works (e.g., inter-architecture similarity increasing with robustness; universally converging representations of matter) only in passing. 'Representation alignment' here means a generic comparison between two representation spaces, not the convergence hypothesis. The BERT-Tiny checkpoint is prajjwal1/bert-tiny, though the paper cites TinyBERT (distillation); this is a minor subject detail for R4.

versions.untested_parts: No systematic scale or capability sweep, and no measure of independently trained models’ distance alignment as scale or performance changes.
CLIP image and caption representations are compared, but the study does not compare models at different capability or training levels to test whether cross-modal alignment rises.
No comparison across random seeds or analysis of shared features or subspaces.
The study aligns mapper-graph layouts; it does not test representational interchangeability by mapping activations, stitching layers, or using relative representations.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
No comparison of convergence results across similarity metrics, metric settings, input choices, or out-of-distribution data.
The study describes local structural differences, but does not test whether overall alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: BERT-base, final layer, epoch 2 vs BERT-base, final layer, epoch 6
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on STREUSLE for 2 versus 6 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Compared mapper-graph organization and local correspondences for representations from the two training epochs.

conditions.value: ℓ2-norm filter; 50 intervals; 50% overlap; DBSCAN min_samples = 3

rows.measure: Topological organization and local alignment patterns in the mapper graphs
rows.value: Epoch 6 representations showed clearer separation between semantic categories; local alignments largely preserved the epoch-6 structure while fragmenting several epoch-2 components. The default analysis produced 78 alignment pairs.
rows.note: This is a qualitative topological comparison, not a scale-dependent distance-similarity measure.

rows.subject: BERT-base, layer 3 vs BERT-base, layer 12
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on STREUSLE for six epochs
rows.operation_detail: Compared mapper-graph organization and local correspondences between layers.
rows.measure: Topological organization of contextualized word representations
rows.value: Layer 3 grouped instances primarily by surface form; layer 12 showed clearer category-based separation. The paper describes local correspondences in which same-word groupings reorganize into semantic-category groupings.
rows.note: The result concerns organization across layers of one model, not convergence across independently trained models.

rows.subject: BERT-base, layer 7 vs BERT-base, layer 12
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on STREUSLE for six epochs
rows.operation_detail: Compared mapper-graph organization and local correspondences between layers.
rows.measure: Topological organization and local alignment patterns
rows.value: Layer 7 already showed substantial semantic organization, but categories were distributed across multiple components; by layer 12, same-label words consolidated into more unified category-specific structures.
rows.locator: Sec. 6.1.2; Fig. 8 and Appendix C, Fig. 13
rows.note: This is a within-model layer comparison, not a test of any listed convergence version.

rows.subject: BERT-base vs BERT-Tiny, final layers
rows.stage_stated: Both fine-tuned on STREUSLE for six epochs
rows.operation_detail: Compared mapper-graph organization and selected local structures across model sizes.
rows.measure: Topological organization and local correspondences between model representations
rows.value: BERT-Tiny was described as having more entangled label structures than BERT-base. The paper also reports selected local cases, including one where BERT-base reached 100% prediction accuracy and BERT-Tiny 58%.
rows.note: The accuracy figures are reported as context for selected structures, not as an alignment metric; the study does not measure an overall alignment-versus-size trend.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. There is only one size pair, fine-tuned on one task, with a qualitative description ('more entangled label structures'). There is no alignment score that could show a size trend. The 100% vs 58% accuracies are case-level prediction accuracies for one selected structure, not alignment values.

rows.subject: CLIP image modality vs CLIP caption modality
rows.operation_detail: Compared mapper graphs for paired image and caption representations produced by CLIP.

conditions.value: 5,000 MS COCO validation images, each paired with a selected caption
Caption with highest image-caption cosine similarity selected for each image
Image-caption cosine distance filter; 50 intervals; 50% overlap; DBSCAN min_samples = 3

rows.measure: Global mapper-graph structure and local cross-modal correspondences
rows.value: The modalities were described as having similar global structures but notable local differences. The paper identified 24 local alignments: 8 one-to-one, 5 fan-in, 6 fan-out, and 3 vanishing patterns; it also describes modality-specific differences in semantic granularity and concept grouping.
rows.note: This is a qualitative analysis of one CLIP setup, not a comparison across model capability levels or a distance-similarity scaling test.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. A single jointly trained CLIP model gives no capability variation for V2. The 24 local alignments are counts of pattern types from the authors' clustering, not a convergence measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
